concept: Quantum annealing is schedule-based analog evolution for optimization-like Hamiltonians
summary: Quantum annealing uses quantum fluctuations, commonly through transverse-field-style terms, to explore optimization landscapes while annealing toward a classical cost Hamiltonian. It is related to but not identical with gate-model time-evolution product formulas.
limitations: Annealing targets optimization or ground-state preparation rather than generic unitary time evolution.
Hardware and schedule constraints matter strongly.
OpenQEvo needs a project-scope decision before implementing annealing as a native method.
implications: Do not force annealing into the current terms/t execution helper.
Represent annealing recommendations as planned or non-executable until a schedule API exists.
Separate annealing primitives from full optimization workflow ownership.

evidence.note: Reviews quantum annealing as an optimization and analog quantum computation framework using quantum fluctuations.
Distinguishes AQC, stoquastic AQC, and quantum annealing settings in a broader adiabatic computing review.
